title: Harira
description: My Thermomix take on a Mourad Lahlou-style harira — a fragrant Moroccan chickpea and lentil soup with warming spices, tomato and fresh herbs.
intro: This is my independent Thermomix homage to Mourad Lahlou and the comforting depth of harira. It keeps the spirit of the original inspiration, but the method is written fresh for TM6 and TM7 cooks who want clear settings and a warming, achievable result.
ingredients: 200 g canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
30 g fresh coriander leaves, plus extra to serve
Salt and black pepper, to taste
steps: Place onion, garlic and fresh herbs (reserve a few coriander leaves for garnish) in the mixing bowl. Chop 5 sec / speed 7.
Add olive oil and sauté 3 min / 120°C / speed 1.
Add cumin, cinnamon, ginger, turmeric, tomato paste and crushed tomatoes. Cook 5 min / 100°C / speed 2.
Add red lentils, chickpeas and vegetable stock. Cook 25 min / 100°C / speed 1 with the simmering basket on the lid instead of the measuring cup to prevent splashing.
Blend lightly 10 sec / speed 3 for a slightly textured consistency, or leave as-is for a chunkier soup.
Season with salt, pepper and lemon juice. Serve in warm bowls with a scatter of fresh coriander.
tips: Red lentils break down beautifully, thickening the soup naturally — no need for flour.
The simmering basket on the lid stops hot soup splashing out during the long cook.
Harira reheats brilliantly the next day; the flavours deepen overnight.

faq.q: Is this the original Mourad Lahlou recipe?
faq.a: No. This is Chef Aly's independent Thermomix reinterpretation inspired by Mourad Lahlou and harira; it is not endorsed by or affiliated with the chef.

faq.q: Can I make this Harira in a TM6 or TM7?
faq.a: Yes. The method is written with TM6 and TM7 settings, using metric weights, clear times, temperatures and speeds.

faq.q: Can I use dried chickpeas instead of canned?
faq.a: Yes — soak 80 g dried chickpeas overnight, then add them 10 minutes earlier at step 4 so they have time to become tender.
